rows.reference_reason: Epilepsy and the epileptic morning jerks on 10 January support the 90-day predicate.
rows.observed_reason: Alex has documented epilepsy at the index date (15 January 2025) and daytime staring spells, interpreted as focal impaired-awareness seizures (epileptic), occurred within the 90-day lookback timeframe (most recently on 13 January 2025).

rows.reference_reason: The visit account treats both recurring patterns as epileptic and documents overlap.
rows.observed_reason: Two distinct patterns interpreted as epileptic (daytime staring spells regarded as focal impaired-awareness seizures, and morning jerks regarded as epileptic) were active with overlapping active intervals recurring during December 2024 and January 2025, within the 90-day lookback timeframe.

rows.reference_reason: A deferred addition is not use, but the letter does not establish whether lamotrigine was started earlier in the 180-day period.
rows.observed_reason: Adding lamotrigine was discussed and deferred at the consultation, confirming it was not initiated then, but the letter lacks a complete inventory or explicit evidence of non-initiation covering the full 180-day timeframe.

rows.reference_reason: The sole EEG requested in the period has not been performed and has no result at T1.
rows.observed_reason: There is a complete request inventory confirming that the routine EEG requested on 15 January 2025 is the only EEG requested since 20 July 2024 (the entire 180-day lookback timeframe), and it has not yet been performed with no result available by the index date.

rows.reference_reason: No explicit revision or complete negative revision history is supplied by T1.
rows.observed_reason: No previously documented epileptic event or pattern was reinterpreted as non-epileptic, and the absence of an explicit revision alone is indeterminate.
